title: Keep the health check inside its time budget

blocks.text: The service's `/health` endpoint checks Postgres, Redis, Kafka and S3, each on its own thread, and the load balancer gives up on the endpoint after two seconds, so the whole check has to fit in that budget. During last night's Kafka outage two things went wrong. Most requests to `/health` answered "all passed" after two seconds while Kafka was unreachable. A few never answered at all, and the load balancer took the instance out of rotation.
`run(...)` starts the probes and builds the report. Finish `await(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/HealthCheck.java`: the wait for one probe, against the deadline the whole check shares.
When you're done, a probe still running at the deadline is reported as timed out, and `/health` answers within its budget however the time left is spread over the probes. About three lines.

cases.says: probes that finish within the budget are reported as passed, in the order given
a probe whose thread is still running at the deadline is reported as timed out, not as passed
with the budget spent, or less than a millisecond of it left, a hung probe is not waited for

origin.section: join(millis) Returns Without Saying Why, So Ask isAlive()

concepts: join(millis) returns the same way whether or not the thread ended, so the caller asks isAlive() (or uses join(Duration)'s answer) before treating the work as done.
join(0) waits forever, including when a deadline's remaining time rounds down to 0 ms; join(Duration) with zero or less only checks.
